The notification links four elements in one official record: the approving department, the requesting government, the requested quantity and the estimated value. That specificity makes the document a useful baseline for tracking whether the proposal changes or advances. ## The procedural boundary

The document consistently describes the matter as a possible or proposed sale and presents itself as a congressional notification. [United States Department of State](https://www.state.gov/releases/bureau-of-political-military-affairs/2026/08/italy-guidance-section-single-variant-air-to-air-advanced-precision-kill-weapon-system-ii/). Its approval language therefore does not, by itself, establish a concluded agreement, a contract award, a completed transaction, delivery or operational use. [United States Department of State](https://www.state.gov/releases/bureau-of-political-military-affairs/2026/08/italy-guidance-section-single-variant-air-to-air-advanced-precision-kill-weapon-system-ii/). The $364 million figure should likewise be read as the estimated total cost attached to the possible sale, not as proof that this amount has been spent, received or booked. ## What would establish the next phase

A later official record would need to confirm that the process advanced beyond the notification stage before readers could describe the transaction as completed or implemented. Such evidence could take the form of an official confirmation of a concluded agreement, a contract award, a delivery or another clearly identified implementation step.
